title: How to procure a custom dataset
summary: From the first brief to the final delivery: how to define, evaluate and source data for the model you are building.
body_markdown:
A dataset request often begins with a volume: hours of speech, video clips or labelled images. That gives a collection a size, but leaves much of the work undefined. Who should the data represent? What conditions should it capture? What needs to arrive alongside the files for your team to use them? Procuring a custom dataset means turning those questions into a specification, then checking that the delivered data meets it.


At Luel, our network of 900,000+ contributors supports the collection of audio, video and image data. You can browse the[data marketplace](https://www.luel.ai/marketplace) or[open a request](https://www.luel.ai/request) for a sample, a licensed dataset or a custom collection. The right starting point depends on what you need and how much of it already exists.


## Define the data around the task


Start by describing what you are building and where it needs to work. A speech model for customer calls needs a different collection from a voice reading long passages aloud. An image model used in a warehouse needs examples of the objects, lighting and camera positions it will encounter there. Those conditions should shape the brief before you choose a collection size.


Be specific about the coverage you need. For speech, that might mean a particular dialect, a range of speakers and recordings made on phones. For video, it could mean people completing named tasks, with a defined camera position and the full action in frame. Separate essential requirements from preferences so a supplier can explain what is feasible and where the scope may need to change.


Include the output your team expects: file formats, labels, transcripts and metadata. If you need speaker identifiers or timestamps, put them in the brief. Add your target volume, budget range and delivery date, including whether a smaller first batch would be useful.


## Check what already exists


Before commissioning a collection, compare your requirements with available datasets. An existing set may cover the whole task, or provide a starting point that a smaller custom collection can extend. Review its documentation and a sample against the same brief you would send for new data.


Custom collection is useful when an important requirement remains uncovered: a language variety, a recording environment, a specialist task or a particular mix of participants. Identify that gap clearly. It gives the collection a purpose and makes it easier to assess whether the proposed scope addresses it.


## Use a pilot to test the brief


For a new collection, ask for a pilot before committing to the full volume. It should follow the proposed instructions and include the conditions that matter to your task. A polished example can show what is possible; a pilot helps you assess whether the collection process produces what you need.


Review the content and run it through your ingestion pipeline. Check whether files load, labels are consistent and the metadata supports your intended use. For speech, listen as well as reading the transcripts. For video, watch complete sequences rather than judging isolated frames.


Use that review to agree acceptance criteria. Define which defects require correction or replacement, how quality will be checked and what happens when a batch falls short. Background noise, for example, may belong in a conversational dataset while being unsuitable for a clean voice corpus. Quality has to be defined for the task.


## Agree the terms and the handover


Ask for documentation of where the data came from, how it was collected and what permissions support its intended use. Review the licence against your planned training, evaluation and commercial use, and clarify any restrictions on sharing or redistribution before committing.


The quote should also make clear what the price covers: collection, annotation, quality checks, delivery and any agreed rework. Confirm whether volume means raw submissions or accepted data, and agree milestones and a review period. At delivery, check the files and documentation against the specification and keep a record of the version your team accepts.


## How to request a custom dataset from Luel


To procure a custom dataset from Luel,[open a data request](https://www.luel.ai/request) with your use case and the requirements you have defined. Include the modality, target coverage, volume, annotation needs, intended use, budget and timeline. If you have found a relevant marketplace listing, reference it and explain what else you need.


You do not need every detail settled to begin the conversation. A clear account of what you are building, what data you already have and what is missing gives the request a useful starting point.
